Q: What should a Multipart HTTP request with multiple file inputs look like? A:

I am maintaining a similar, but more in-depth answer at What does enctype='multipart/form-data' mean?.

To see exactly what is happening, use nc -l and a user agent like a browser or cURL.

Save the form to an .html file:

<form action="http://localhost:8000" method="post" enctype="multipart/form-data">
  <p><input type="text" name="text" value="text default">
  <p><input type="file" name="file1">
  <p><input type="file" name="file2">
  <p><button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>

Create files to upload:

echo 'Content of a.txt.' > a.txt
echo '<!DOCTYPE html><title>Content of a.html.</title>' > a.html

Run:

nc -l localhost 8000

Open the HTML on your browser, select the files and click on submit and check the terminal.

nc prints the request received. Firefox sent:

POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8000
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Ubuntu; Linux i686; rv:29.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/29.0
Accept: text/html,application/xhtml+xml,application/xml;q=0.9,*/*;q=0.8
Accept-Language: en-US,en;q=0.5
Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate
Cookie: __atuvc=34%7C7; permanent=0; _gitlab_session=226ad8a0be43681acf38c2fab9497240; __profilin=p%3Dt; request_method=GET
Connection: keep-alive
Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=---------------------------9051914041544843365972754266
Content-Length: 554

-----------------------------9051914041544843365972754266
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="text"

text default
-----------------------------9051914041544843365972754266
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file1"; filename="a.txt"
Content-Type: text/plain

Content of a.txt.

-----------------------------9051914041544843365972754266
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file2"; filename="a.html"
Content-Type: text/html

<!DOCTYPE html><title>Content of a.html.</title>

-----------------------------9051914041544843365972754266--

Alternatively, cURL should send the same POST request as your a browser form:

nc -l localhost 8000
curl -F "text=default" -F "file1=@a.txt" -F "file2=@a.html" localhost:8000

You can do multiple tests with:

while true; do printf '' | nc -l localhost 8000; done

Q: Ansible :Unable to parse /etc/ansible/hosts as an inventory source A:

It can be as simple as change of location of inventory file. Make sure to validate your $HOME/.ansible.cfg file entry inventory points to a valid inventory file.

Q: Is it possible to include files (linking) based on a component property? A:

You can use the {$IFDEF youridentifier} optional code {$ENDIF} method to conditionally compile data in to your application and then to enable it just go to your project options and enter youridentifier into the appropriate option field. Another method of doing this is to add the following to the top of your unit (or in an include file):

{$DEFINE youridentifier}

which will force youridentifier on. To disable, just place a period right before the $:

{.$DEFINE youridentifier}

Using these techniques its easy to conditionally bring in code or replace code with each compile.

EDIT:
You can also use dependency injection.

First in a globally shared unit in your application, add the following:

type
  ISupportDrivers = interface
    ['{E9951C77-C208-4257-8BEB-AA30D5FCDF66}']
    procedure bind(aComponent:TComponent);
  end;

var
  gSupportedDrivers : ISupportDrivers = nil;

in your main application, or data module, use this unit and add the following check. OnCreate is likely a good place:

if gSupportedDrivers <> nil then
  gSupportedDrivers.bind(self);  // or other specific class if you need it.

The parameter is actually completely optional, but it gives you the ability to walk the component children to manipulate properties.

Now, in the unit that contains all of the drivers or code you want to add in the uses clause, implement the interface in a simple class like so (can all be in the implementation!):

type
  TBindings = class(TInterfacedObject,ISupportDrivers)
  public
    procedure bind(aComponent:TComponent);
  end;

procedure TBindings.bind(aComponent:TComponent)
begin
  // wire up you component changes.
end;

initialization
  gSupportedDrivers := TBindings.Create;
end;

then place an {$IFDEF SUPPORT} around the use of this unit in your dpr and make sure the other units you don't want linked are either in the ifdef area, or are only used by your concrete TBindings unit. Your component won't have to recompile, your just assigning properties at runtime. The TBindings unit will recompile, but it's so small it really shouldn't matter by itself.

Q: Python dataframe drop rows which occur less frequently A:

I believe this code should give you what you want.

df.loc[df.groupby('name').transform('size').ge(2)]

or

df.loc[df['name'].map(df['name'].value_counts().ge(2))]

Old answer:

df['count'] = df.groupby('name').transform('count')
df2 = df.loc[df['count'] >= 2].drop(columns='count')
